findings.finding: 50 known neutral field occurrences remain blank because entire mixed-actor blocks are protected: CR-180 participant name/contact block plus printed signer name (8perfixture); CR-181 participant name/contact and neutral county/case/party captions (12perfixture); CR-106 county/case/case-name/repeated case caption and known primary-document identification (5perfixture).
findings.sourceRole: CR-180/181 print ATTORNEY OR PARTY WITHOUT ATTORNEY; CR-180 printed name is distinct from signature. CR-106 neutral captions/document description are distinct from server identity and completed service.
findings.repair: Create exact source-field mappings for held neutral facts. Keep lawyer-only bar/firm fields and actual signatures, service acts, judge findings/grant-denial/order dates blank. Do not substitute participant identity/address for an unheld server. Correct guide instructions to leave only actual court-owned fields blank.

findings.finding: The guide commands Fill in every blank listed below and enumerates all six unrelated CR-180 dismissal narratives/date fields, including human-trafficking proof and section1000.3 dismissal date, for every reduction participant. It also requires all mail and personal-service recipient rows without selected-service/actual-recipient conditions. Court street/mailing/cityZIP caption blanks are refused as court-owned and omitted from participant handback even though the court destination must be supplied. CR-106 server address fields whose internal names include AppellantLawyer are incorrectly attorney-only, not the source-printed server home/business address.

findings.repair: Model only the applicable supported dismissal basis, optional interests-of-justice narrative, trafficking/deferred-entry conditions, selected service method and actual recipients. Require unknown court location and server contact handback without inventing values. Unused branches and rows must remain truthfully not applicable; do not demand trafficking evidence or a deferred-entry date from every17(b)/17(d)(2) participant.

findings.finding: Sign and date each form yourself conflicts with court-owned CR-181 and the source-identified CR-106 server; guide does not distinguish petition signer/server/judge. It says service method is not established although held CR-106 explicitly covers mail or personal delivery and directs electronic service to POS-050/EFS-050. It further invents filing date as the anchor for the registry’s15-day notice requirement, whose quoted rule does not identify that anchor.
findings.sourceQuote: CR-106: This form is for proof of service by mail or personal delivery. For proof of electronic service, use Proof of Electronic Service (form POS-050/EFS-050).
findings.repair: Separate participant petition signature, adult server completion and judge signature; preserve source prerequisites and post-service completion. State source-supported CR-106 scope and retain local-method inquiry where needed. Do not make an unsupported15-days-before-filing deadline; bind timing to the applicable supported notice event or obtain that specific court instruction.

findings.finding: Participant instructions expose internal AcroForm identifiers and repository/manifest/registry implementation prose throughout, including rows named Page1[0]... and instructions framed as deterministic review fixtures/committed-manifest words.
findings.repair: Keep internal identifiers and technical provenance in review evidence; provide plain source labels, applicable action/actor and conditions in participant copy. Separate reviewer-only fixture provenance from the delivered participant guide.

findings.finding: The new input evaluator accepts offenseType="banana" as READY despite the source requiring felony, misdemeanor or infraction. It also accepts a sparse3-slot array containing only row3 as READY: forEach/every skip missing rows, violating complete per-offense bundle validation.
